1259323.assayname: Primary screen of kinases in signalling pathway between Protease activated receptor 2 (PAR2) and the ion channels Transient receptor potential vanilloid-4 (TRPV4) in HEK293 cells
1259323.assaydescription: Protease-activated receptor 2 (PAR2) is a proinflammatory G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) which is activated by inflammatory proteases and its activation initiates signalling pathways that modulate the non-selective cation channel transient receptor potential vanilloid-4 (TRPV4). PAR2-dependent opening of TRPV4 has been attributed to kinase activation but the identity of the responsible enzymes is unknown. Deciphering the signalling pathways involved in the PAR2-dependent opening of TRPV4 may yield new targets for the pain treatment. This study has identified specific kinases involved in opening TRPV4, using a selective screen of siRNA SMARTpools which individually targeted all human kinases, in HEK293 cells that stably express inducible TRPV4. This screen is unique because it uses a real-time assay measuring intracellular calcium with Fura-2AM dye. From the primary screen, subsequent validation screen and on-target mRNA expression analysis we identified two kinases as crucial to the PAR2-dependent opening of TRPV4 in HEK293 cells, MAPK13 and WNK4. In conclusion, this study describes a powerful new application of siRNA knockdown to identity signalling molecules responsible for the PAR2-dependent opening of TRPV4 which will help elucidate this signalling process.

Compounds 4b, 5a, 5b and 5d exhibited promising growth inhibitions and thus were further tested in advanced 5-dose testing assay to determine their GI50 values. The cellular based assay results revealed that 3,5-bis-trifluoromethylphenyl (5b) urea member is the best derivative with superior potency and efficacy compared to sorafenib as well as notable extended spectrum activity covering 57 human cancer cell lines. Moreover, the most potent derivatives in cells were investigated for their RAF inhibitory activities, and the results were rationalized with the molecular docking study.
